## Module to write
path: ServerScriptService/GrowthModels.luau
purpose: Feature: Visible plot growth, split into SMALL modules (each well under 200 lines; the coder's output cap was hit by a single big file last time). The plot is a big empty floor and buying upgrades barely changes how it looks. (1) ServerScriptService/GrowthModels.luau: pure model builders, one short function per kind, each returning a Model built from 3-8 anchored parts in the given theme colors (never default grey): dropperMachine(cf, theme), chevrons(cf, theme), orePile(cf, theme, tierColor), vault(cf, theme, label), plotWall(plotCFrame, size, theme). (2) ServerScriptService/PlotGrowth.luau: the service. PlotGrowth.apply(player, plot, ownedIds) builds the missing models for every owned upgrade (Dropper 2/3/4 -> dropperMachine on the dropper row above the conveyor; Speed 1/2 -> chevrons along the conveyor; ore tiers -> orePile beside the collector; Cash x1.5/x2 -> vault next to the collector; any purchase -> plotWall around the plot edge), each popping in with GameAssets.popIn plus GameAssets.burst. PlotGrowth.clear(player) shrinks and removes them on rebirth. Bump counter plot_growth_built per model. Hook: UpgradeService calls PlotGrowth.apply after every successful purchase and on plot claim; RebirthService calls PlotGrowth.clear after a rebirth reset. -- Pure model builders with no side effects and no telemetry, kept under 180 lines. Exports dropperMachine(cf, theme), chevrons(cf, theme), orePile(cf, theme, tierColor), vault(cf, theme, label) and plotWall(plotCFrame, size, theme). Each is one short function that returns a Model of 3-8 anchored parts (Anchored=true, CanCollide=false except wall posts, CanTouch=false), colored only from the theme colors or tierColor (theme.accent, theme.primary, theme.floor, with fallbacks to GameAssets palette), never default grey. Includes a tiny local helper mk(parent, size, cf, color, material, shape) that creates a part. vault builds a box body, a door and a billboard TextLabel with the label. plotWall builds low corner posts and rails around the edge of the given size without blocking the buy pads or claim gate (rails are thin and low, posts at the corners and at intervals). Requires only ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets for the palette fallbacks. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: plot_growth_built.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/GameAssets.luau

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price. Chain the first few upgrades so there is always something affordable to chase in the first minute, with no long dead gaps.
- Starting cash must be strictly below the first upgrade's price, never equal to it. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s. Check starter cash against the first cost in config before finishing.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. A highlight or "affordable" counter above 0 with no purchase counter means the pad was reachable in logic but the player never touched it. Put the first pad close to where the player stands after claiming (just off the walking path), and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad, button, shop purchase or rebirth attempted without enough cash, or a shop card whose requirement is not owned, needs a red flash, an audible buzz, a shake and a "Need $N" or requirement toast, debounced to about 1s. Never return silently from a denied Buy handler. A silent denial confuses young players.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback must fire within about 3-5s, never 20s. A spec or acceptance text that says 20s is wrong for playtests, so shorten it and keep the tested window consistent. Claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall. A tutorial_reshown counter above 0 means a step stalled. Give a clear objective from second 0, make the steps lead the player to every key feature (buy pad, shop), and check that the guide beam or arrow actually appears (its census count is above 0). If the census shows beams = 0, the guide is invisible: fix the beam creation (attachments, parenting, target lookup), not just its config.
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.
- Shared effect helpers (burst, shake, sound, FOV punch) only matter if gameplay code calls them. Wire each helper to a real event (collect, buy, rebirth, big upgrade) and check that its counter is above 0 after a playtest. Big moments deserve stronger feedback than routine ones: camera shake, a shockwave ring, or a larger popup. The purchase is the biggest reward moment, so make sure it has a visible and audible effect and a counter. Fire milestone effects only at milestone counts, not on every event. Make the routine collect reward escalate too (bigger burst or louder sound as streaks or tiers grow), so identical feedback for every cube doesn't flatten the loop.
- Keep routine per-event effects cheap and rate-limited. One sound and one burst per cash-in, at most a few per second per player, and reuse a single Sound object where possible. Do not create a new Sound plus several emitters for every cube. Rate limits and cooldowns must apply only to routine effects. Never let them swallow milestone effects, which must fire exactly when the count hits the milestone

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.

--!nonstrict
-- GrowthModels: pure model builders for visible plot growth (no side effects, no telemetry).
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local okGA, GameAssets = pcall(function()
	return require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GameAssets", 10))
end)
if not okGA then
	GameAssets = nil
end

local GrowthModels = {}

local FALLBACKS = {
	accent = Color3.fromRGB(255, 200, 40),
	primary = Color3.fromRGB(80, 170, 255),
	floor = Color3.fromRGB(120, 220, 140),
}

-- Resolve a theme color, falling back to GameAssets.Palette, then a bright default (never grey).
local function themeColor(theme: any, key: string): Color3
	if type(theme) == "table" and typeof(theme[key]) == "Color3" then
		return theme[key]
	end
	if GameAssets and type(GameAssets.Palette) == "table" then
		local c = GameAssets.Palette[key]
		if typeof(c) == "Color3" then
			return c
		end
	end
	return FALLBACKS[key] or FALLBACKS.accent
end

local function mk(parent: Instance, size: Vector3, cf: CFrame, color: Color3, material: Enum.Material?, shape: Enum.PartType?): Part
	local p = Instance.new("Part")
	p.Anchored = true
	p.CanCollide = false
	p.CanTouch = false
	p.CanQuery = false
	p.CastShadow = true
	p.TopSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	p.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	p.Shape = shape or Enum.PartType.Block
	p.Size = size
	p.CFrame = cf
	p.Color = color
	p.Material = material or Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
	p.Parent = parent
	return p
end

local function newModel(name: string): Model
	local m = Instance.new("Model")
	m.Name = name
	return m
end

local UPRIGHT = CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.pi / 2) -- turns an X-axis cylinder upright

function GrowthModels.dropperMachine(cf: CFrame, theme: any): Model
	local primary, accent, floor = themeColor(theme, "primary"), themeColor(theme, "accent"), themeColor(theme, "floor")
	local m = newModel("DropperMachine")
	local base = mk(m, Vector3.new(5, 1, 5), cf * CFrame.new(0, 0.5, 0), primary, Enum.Material.Metal)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(3.6, 3.4, 3.6), cf * CFrame.new(0, 2.7, 0), accent, Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(0.8, 2.6, 2.6), cf * CFrame.new(0, 5.4, 0) * UPRIGHT, floor, Enum.Material.Metal, Enum.PartType.Cylinder)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(1.4, 1, 1), cf * CFrame.new(0, 1.4, -1.9) * UPRIGHT, primary, Enum.Material.Metal, Enum.PartType.Cylinder)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(3.8, 0.4, 3.8), cf * CFrame.new(0, 4.6, 0), accent, Enum.Material.Neon)
	m.PrimaryPart = base
	return m
end

function GrowthModels.chevrons(cf: CFrame, theme: any): Model
	local accent, primary = themeColor(theme, "accent"), themeColor(theme, "primary")
	local m = newModel("Chevrons")
	local len = 2.4
	local s = math.sin(math.rad(45))
	local first: Part? = nil
	-- apex points along cf.LookVector, arms trail behind (+Z)
	for i = 0, 2 do
		local color = (i % 2 == 0) and accent or primary
		local apex = cf * CFrame.new(0, 0.15, i * 3.2 - 3.2)
		for _, side in ipairs({ 1, -1 }) do
			local rot = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(45) * side, 0)
			local center = apex * CFrame.new(side * s * len / 2, 0, s * len / 2) * rot
			local p = mk(m, Vector3.new(0.7, 0.2, len), center, color, Enum.Material.Neon)
			first = first or p
		end
	end
	m.PrimaryPart = first
	return m
end

function GrowthModels.orePile(cf: CFrame, theme: any, tierColor: Color3?): Model
	local tier = (typeof(tierColor) == "Color3") and tierColor or themeColor(theme, "accent")
	local floor = themeColor(theme, "floor")
	local m = newModel("OrePile")
	local base = mk(m, Vector3.new(0.6, 5, 5), cf * CFrame.new(0, 0.3, 0) * UPRIGHT, floor, Enum.Material.Slate, Enum.PartType.Cylinder)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(2.6, 2.2, 2.6), cf * CFrame.new(0, 1.4, 0) * CFrame.Angles(0.3, 0.6, 0.2), tier, Enum.Material.Slate)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(2, 1.8, 2), cf * CFrame.new(1.3, 1, 0.8) * CFrame.Angles(0.1, 1.1, 0.4), tier, Enum.Material.Slate)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(1.8, 1.8, 1.8), cf * CFrame.new(-1.2, 0.9, -0.7), tier, Enum.Material.Slate, Enum.PartType.Ball)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(0.9, 2.2, 0.9), cf * CFrame.new(0.1, 3, 0.1) * CFrame.Angles(0.2, 0.4, 0.15), tier, Enum.Material.Neon)
	m.PrimaryPart = base
	return m
end

function GrowthModels.vault(cf: CFrame, theme: any, label: string?): Model
	local primary, accent = themeColor(theme, "primary"), themeColor(theme, "accent")
	local m = newModel("Vault")
	local body = mk(m, Vector3.new(5, 5, 4), cf * CFrame.new(0, 2.5, 0), primary, Enum.Material.Metal)
	body.CanCollide = true
	local door = mk(m, Vector3.new(0.4, 3.4, 3.4), cf * CFrame.new(0, 2.7, -2.1) * CFrame.Angles(math.pi / 2, 0, math.pi / 2), accent, Enum.Material.Metal, Enum.PartType.Cylinder)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(0.5, 0.5, 1.8), cf * CFrame.new(0, 2.7, -2.5), accent, Enum.Material.Neon)
	mk(m, Vector3.new(5.4, 0.5, 4.4), cf * CFrame.new(0, 5.2, 0), accent, Enum.Material.Neon)
	local gui = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	gui.Name = "VaultLabel"
	gui.Size = UDim2.fromScale(7, 2)
	gui.StudsOffset = Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)
	gui.AlwaysOnTop = false
	gui.MaxDistance = 90
	local txt = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	txt.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	txt.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	txt.TextScaled = true
	txt.Font = Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy
	txt.Text = tostring(label or "Vault")
	txt.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	local stroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	stroke.Thickness = 3
	stroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(30, 25, 50)
	stroke.Parent = txt
	txt.Parent = gui
	gui.Parent = door
	m.PrimaryPart = body
	return m
end

function GrowthModels.plotWall(plotCFrame: CFrame, size: any, theme: any): Model
	local accent, primary = themeColor(theme, "accent"), themeColor(theme, "primary")
	local sx, sz = 60, 60
	if typeof(size) == "Vector3" then
		sx, sz = size.X, size.Z
	elseif typeof(size) == "Vector2" then
		sx, sz = size.X, size.Y
	end
	local m = newModel("PlotWall")
	local hx, hz = sx / 2, sz / 2
	local first: Part? = nil
	-- thin low rails along the four edges
	local rails = {
		{ Vector3.new(sx, 0.4, 0.4), Vector3.new(0, 1.2, -hz) },
		{ Vector3.new(sx, 0.4, 0.4), Vector3.new(0, 1.2, hz) },
		{ Vector3.new(0.4, 0.4, sz), Vector3.new(-hx, 1.2, 0) },
		{ Vector3.new(0.4, 0.4, sz), Vector3.new(hx, 1.2, 0) },
	}
	for _, r in ipairs(rails) do
		local p = mk(m, r[1], plotCFrame * CFrame.new(r[2]), accent, Enum.Material.Neon)
		first = first or p
	end
	-- corner posts (solid) and mid-edge posts (decorative, non-colliding)
	local corners = { { -hx, -hz }, { hx, -hz }, { -hx, hz }, { hx, hz } }
	for _, c in ipairs(corners) do
		local post = mk(m, Vector3.new(1.4, 3, 1.4), plotCFrame * CFrame.new(c[1], 1.5, c[2]), primary, Enum.Material.Metal)
		post.CanCollide = true
		mk(m, Vector3.new(1.8, 0.4, 1.8), plotCFrame * CFrame.new(c[1], 3.2, c[2]), accent, Enum.Material.Neon)
	end
	local mids = { { 0, -hz }, { 0, hz }, { -hx, 0 }, { hx, 0 } }
	for _, c in ipairs(mids) do
		mk(m, Vector3.new(0.9, 2, 0.9), plotCFrame * CFrame.new(c[1], 1, c[2]), primary, Enum.Material.Metal)
	end
	m.PrimaryPart = first
	return m
end

return GrowthModels
